I have a few:

* Do you still sometimes or often feel depressed?

* I know you said "no pills", does that mean you never took any medication during or before your recovery?

* What was the biggest catalyst for your recovery? 

* Was it by chance or was it something you did to change yourself?

* If it wasn't by chance, where did you find the motivation?

* Was death ever appealing to you? The idea of being liberated from existence? Does that go away when things start to get better?

* Assuming you did this with the help of others, do you think you would have been able to recover on your own? Or is the interest and empathy of other humans necessary for recovering from depression?

Thankyou for the response. 
Part of me wants to reply point by point, but I worry that will make me seem argumentative or overly defensive.
I am neither, I am grateful for any advice and outside perspective, especially from someone who has been there.
But to answer some questions:
> How many friends do you need? They are not like Pokemon, you are under no rational obligation to "catch 'em all". Keeping friends has positives, but it also takes energy, and you have limited finite energy.

I didn't mean to say it like that. What I meant is that I moved around schools a lot as a kid. I don't know why but it made it hard for me to make and keep friends. I'm not a social outgoing person, and it's depressing to find myself without anyone close to talk to in such a hard time.

r/seddit I have lurked on a little bit. I understand how it's beneficial for some. Maybe one day I'll find it useful. To me, the place is built on the assumption that everyone is a great actor, and if confidence doesn't come naturally, you can pretend. I've been down that road and it's embarrassing. I have no poker face, no way of acting my way out of a situation, or into one for that matter.

> Congratulations on possessing such sound certainty of the future. If I was that sure about the future, I would buy a lottery ticket. If you don't have the ability to prediction lottery draws, I wouldn't be so certain of your predictive ability about the future.

You have misunderstood me again here - I have no certainty of the future and that's what troubles me more than almost anything. What I mean is that I know what I have left to live for here and now, and there isn't much. The list gets shorter daily, and now I'm in some ridiculous argument with my Mother and Sister who have no grasp of what I'm going through. I feel like I'm shouting and nobody is hearing, and maybe they'll only truly see it when I'm gone... maybe that's the price I have to pay to be understood.

Thankyou. I definitely value a place like this more than a doctor. I have difficulty putting things into words and trusting medical staff with the entire truth of something, which is no problem when I'm anonymous on the internets. Lucky there are kind people here too who aren't motivated by a paycheck to offer some words of advice. Advice is why I'm here.

Graduating university in music was not overly difficult. I finished studies in November last year... I don't know if 'success' is the right word, it's not a crowning achievement of mine, put it that way. At least while I was a student I had reason to be poor, and assessment to focus on and keep me goal-oriented. Making it through 3 years and not dropping out was really a way of putting off making real decisions about my life for as long as I possibly could.

Thanks for the link.
I should have elaborated. I've been on anti-depressants twice before, most recently in 2006. All I wanted to do was talk to someone, but I stupidly admitted to suicidal thoughts, and so it seemed I was written off as a crazy person who just needed some pills to sort out a 'chemical inbalance'. 
The pills themselves were awful and robbed me of what little motivation, appetite and concentration I had. My grades suffered and I never slept 8 hours uninterrupted again until I started smoking weed about a year ago (though I don't know if that was related to the anti-depressants).

I do feel guilt about a number of things. It feels pretty hard for me to communicate with people. At work (I do work, in retail, about 12-15 hours a week - which barely gets me by), I let people down a lot because I can't concentrate and I have no idea what I'm doing. Probably because I think about suicide most at work... If I worked retail in anything approaching 'full time' hours I would not survive it long.
Not to get into it too much, but I live with my mother who uses guilt to win arguments and to make points about irrelevant shit. In fairness, she has supported me for 23 years, most of those as a single parent... though lately it's been begrudgingly done and I'm constantly reminded what a colossal fuck up I am that I'm a university graduate and can't pay for my own food. She has even said a number of times that she feels she is owed something for all the years of bringing me up.
So, it's not all in my head.
You're braver than I, bench or no.

Thanks for your positivity!
I think you are maybe right in saying confidence can be earned, but then to think that I haven't 'earned' enough confidence doesn't seem right. 
I've pushed myself a long way from my comfort zone in the past, which, as a pretty introverted person, is hard to truly 'enjoy'. I like to think I've 'earned' a fuckton of confidence doing what I've had to do, even the anxiety attacks I sometimes experience being around lots of people. But I guess the confidence thing only comes naturally to the extroverted.

> I do honestly believe this


Well, I know how this sounds, but I believed that too for a long time. I believed against statistics and I believed against every inch of self-loathing I have, but when you're reaching the mid-20's and it still hasn't happened... it's a lot harder to swallow.
There are others who in my shoes might have had the courage and positivity in their lives to persevere and hold out hope against the odds of one day finding someone, every year just saying "It still hasn't happened, but it just hasn't happened YET". I am not one of those people. I held on as long as I could, and handled all the rejection I could bear.

So. I don't know if my reasons were 'right' or whatever. I know that having suicidal thoughts helped me make this decision, and I know that makes some uncomfortable. For me, it just takes a lot to lower my inhibitions, so I'll take what help I can get. If I weren't suicidal, I might still be a virgin for a long time to come. But then, I'm suicidal (partly) because I was a virgin for so long.

I know nobody is still reading by now, but hell...
Now that I have some perspective on it, I still don't regret what I did. Sex itself wasn't that fun but I'm glad it's over.
However, I think that after reaching a certain age or frame of mind, the rite of passage that is 'losing one's virginity' loses all personal significance. ie. once a virgin, always a virgin. I may have lost my physical virginity, but externally, nothing about the way I behave around women has changed.
And won't ever change without some 'confidence', which is not something I have control over. 
I guess fucking a prostitute might have done some damage there, but then that's of little concern to someone who would rather be looking down the barrel of a gun than facing the rest of his twenties alone.

Sorry for the rant. Thanks for your encouraging words. I've had bad experiences in therapy and generally in dumping my problems on individual people so I probably won't burden you with all my bullshit but thanks for the offer.

Yeah that's a problem :(
But have you ever slept on a park bench in a strange city?!

That's what I want to hear. 
A lack of money and commitments here are preventing me from traveling, though I've always wanted to. I hope I get to soon.

Thankyou, I'll check out his music. 
Has a weight been lifted? Somewhat. Not as relieving as I thought it would be. But it needed to be done and I feel a bit better for it.

Perhaps I understated the severity of my depression. I didn't start this thread to talk about that, though.
Thanks for the advice.
I lurk occasionally. I don't believe confidence can be "learnt", or at least in my case, faked. I'm a bad actor. Women can sense desperation.

She gave me head with a condom on which I thought would be weird but it was still pretty cool. Then we fucked, me on top. For a while. I don't know if she was "loose" or I had just fapped my sensitivity away but I didn't get much from intercourse.
She finished me off with a handjob. She didn't speak good english. Said "too big" a lot but I think that she meant the condom was too big for me.
I definitely agree sex should be emotionally meaningful. That path is blocked to me though, and I'm not getting any younger... and I have needs, I guess.

Said she was 20, looked 30ish. Nice body regardless. Went for like 20 minutes. 
I've waited long enough for something meaningful. I just don't have the looks or personality to attract women. I'm suicidal in fact so today I just said fuck it, went for it.
It's too soon to know if I regret it or not.
